A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JAPS and provide complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching the methods, proofs, tables, figures, and retained reconstruction examples.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-restoration experiments in Tables 1–2, guidance ablations, and synthetic Gaussian-mixture Jacobian diagnostics.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds ImageNet Jacobian diagnostics, controlled posterior-sampling experiments, further ablations, and inference timings.

M1.justification: The coupled direct/proximal surrogates, projection guidance, conditional DDIM update, and nonlinear extension remain unchanged. The DDIM correction highlighted in v3's abstract already appears in v2. Enlarging the synthetic denoiser changes an experimental configuration rather than the proposed JAPS procedure.

E1.justification: ImageNet, CelebA-HQ, and their restoration tasks are retained. Appendix C.3 adds synthetic GMM inverse-problem scenarios with four measurement-operator classes, including underdetermined and square measurements; v2 used the GMM only for denoiser diagnostics.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix C.2 expands the evaluated alternatives to unequal-weight convex mixtures of the direct and proximal surrogates, extending v2's fixed equal-weight mixture comparison.

E3.justification: The reported GMM configuration changes from 32 to 256 dimensions, 128 to 256 hidden channels, two to four residual blocks, and 5,000 to 10,000 training epochs. New protocols include ImageNet Jacobian estimation, a 100-image mixture sweep at fixed guidance scale, ground-truth likelihood/posterior comparisons, and timing measurements. Table 4 also introduces DAPS NFE counts that are not consistently reconciled with Section 4's general 1,000-NFE description.

E4.justification: V3 adds real-backbone Jacobian diagnostics, projection-coefficient trajectories, convex-mixture sensitivity tests, and analytical-versus-trained GMM comparisons using likelihood-score error and posterior distance. These directly investigate the proposed mechanism. The earlier guidance, measurement-noise, stochasticity, step-count, and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 first reports kernel-density distributions of the existing reconstruction metrics, while B.3 introduces stochastic trace estimation for Jacobian asymmetry. Earlier GMM mean/standard-deviation reporting remains. No formal significance test or additional independent training-seed count is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. V3 adds substantial diagnostic, mixture-ablation, GMM posterior/score-error, and timing results; the GMM evidence uses revised settings. Table 4, for example, reports ImageNet nonlinear-blur times of 60.33 seconds for JAPS versus 47.72 for ΠGDM, qualifying universal cost-parity interpretations.

T1.justification: V3 corrects the proximal derivation's conditional mean to include y, adds regularity justification for differentiation under the integral, and introduces nonlinear-remainder and projection-edge-case reasoning. The covariance–Jacobian identity promoted to Proposition 3.3 already appeared in v2's Appendix A.5; the principal identities and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly restrict the direct/proximal bridge to Gaussian approximations and linear or locally linear measurements. The abstract also highlights the already-existing DDIM correction. The principal JAPS, nonlinear-extension, and reconstruction-quality contributions remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.5 explains the one-dimensional projection choice, its relationship to measurement consistency, and behavior near zero or negative projection coefficients. The synthetic experiments support a new ideal-versus-trained interpretation of guidance performance. Section 3.5 and the conclusion more explicitly discuss curvature, Gaussian assumptions, and limits on transferring the derivation to latent models.

D1.justification: V3 adds a JAPS repository link, NVIDIA L40S timing information, and detailed matrix-free Jacobian-estimation procedures with iteration counts, probe counts, and sampling instructions. These substantially extend reproducibility information beyond v2's existing training and baseline details. The appendix nevertheless retains the earlier statement that code will be released upon acceptance.

R1.justification: The bibliography and principal positioning against direct and proximal samplers are retained. The DDIM correction emphasized in v3's abstract was already contrasted with previous methods in v2 Section 3.4; no new cited research or novelty relationship is introduced.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted rewrites in Sections 3.2, 3.4, and 3.5, introduces explanatory subsection headings, and reorders appendix proofs. Author affiliations, publication information, and acknowledgments also change. The overall main-text and Appendix A–E organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 redraws Figure 2, adds Figures 5–9 and timing Table 4, and substantially expands the graphical presentation of diagnostics and supplementary analyses. Earlier sensitivity plots and reconstruction galleries are retained with relocation or renumbering; the gallery images themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2's explanation of trained-Jacobian harm relied mainly on toy diagnostics and reconstruction ablations. V3 substantially strengthens that central mechanism with real-backbone diagnostics and controlled analytical-versus-trained posterior experiments, supported by mixture tests and reproducibility details. Clearer assumptions and proof corrections improve precision. The violin plots do not establish statistical significance, and the timing results qualify cost-parity claims, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
